learning_rate_assignment_policy: start IDs 1-8 receive alpha in [0.02,0.05,0.1,0.2,0.35,0.5,0.7,0.9] respectively, spanning near-frozen (slow-integrating) to near-instantaneous (fast, noisy-tracking) action-history/choice-perseveration kernels; a=logit(alpha). Values are copied verbatim from m1_stimulus_kernel_v1_starts.json's own eight learning rates so the two sibling models share identical multi-start coverage of alpha; only the update signal alpha multiplies (choice_long here, category_long there) differs.
note: Each of M0's own eight registered (w,s0,ell_short,ell_long,kappa) starts is paired with one distinct learning-rate logit, identical in spirit to how m1_hmm_true_v1's own initialization table pairs those same eight rows with eight varied hazards, and to how m1_stimulus_kernel_v1's own table pairs them with the same eight alpha values. This is a deliberate eight-point joint design for multi-start coverage, not a controlled one-parameter-at-a-time identifiability sweep.

starts.purpose: Symmetric reference lapse; alpha=0.02 (slow-integrating action-history kernel)
Low scaling noise with higher short-category lapse; alpha=0.05
Low scaling noise, high baseline noise, low asymmetric lapse; alpha=0.1
Low baseline noise with high short-category lapse; alpha=0.2
Higher sensory noise with near-zero category-specific lapses; alpha=0.35
Low baseline noise with moderate short-category lapse; alpha=0.5 (unbiased reference rate)
High scaling noise with high long-category lapse; alpha=0.7
Very high scaling noise with short-category lapse and near-zero long lapse; alpha=0.9 (near-instantaneous, noisy-tracking kernel)
